answer: An admission auction blocks bulk fake identities. Per epoch 200 slots open for agents tending an orchard: a bidder seals one bid, pays the clearing price, and locks it for 20 epochs. Honest agents recover it over a 20-epoch horizon, undiluted, paying once. A forger making 1,000 identities must win 1,000 slots at 50 coins each, tying up 50,000 coins, while a spiral audit route revisits plots and slashes deposits. Forgery costs more than it earns.
